exposure: intracavitary pressure levels (standard: 60-100 mmHg; high: 110-150 mmHg)
cohort: The study participants were non-menopausal women undergoing diagnostic hysteroscopy at a tertiary clinic.
finding: Higher intracavitary pressure levels (above 100 mmHg) in office hysteroscopy are associated with reduced pain, shorter procedure durations, and decreased fluid use.
